es.B: Entonces Job respondió:
es.R: Entonces Job dijo:

fr.L: Et Job répondit et dit :
fr.B: Alors Job répondit :
fr.R: Alors Job a dit :

sw.L: Ndipo Ayubu akajibu, akasema:
sw.B: Kisha Ayubu akajibu:
sw.R: Kisha Ayubu akasema:

vi.B: Bấy giờ Gióp đáp:
vi.R: Gióp nói:

ko.L: 그러자 욥이 대답하여 말했다.
ko.B: 그러자 욥이 대답했다.
ko.R: 그러자 욥이 말했다.

decisions.choice: Job answers Bildad
decisions.reason: This is Job's reply to Bildad's first speech (chapter 8). As in 3:1-2, 4:1, 6:1 and 8:1, the words that introduce a speech are prose; the speech itself (9:2-10:22) is poetry.

decisions.choice: answered (Balanced), said (Readable), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs, "answered and said". Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say it once, with the same wording at every speech introduction in Job.

source.text: אָ֭מְנָם יָדַ֣עְתִּי כִי־כֵ֑ן וּמַה־יִּצְדַּ֖ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Truly I know that [it is] so; and how can be in the right a mortal with God?

en.L: Truly I know that [it is] so; \q and how can a mortal be in the right with God?
en.B: Yes, I know that it is so; \q but how can a mortal be in the right before God?
en.R: Yes, I know this is true. \q But how can any human being win a case against God?

es.L: En verdad sé que [es] así; \q ¿y cómo puede un mortal tener la razón frente a Dios?
es.B: Sí, sé que es así; \q pero ¿cómo puede un mortal salir con la razón ante Dios?
es.R: Sí, sé que esto es verdad. \q Pero ¿cómo puede un ser humano ganarle un juicio a Dios?

fr.L: Vraiment, je sais qu’[il en est] ainsi ; \q et comment un mortel serait-il dans son droit face à Dieu ?
fr.B: Oui, je sais qu’il en est ainsi ; \q mais comment un mortel aurait-il gain de cause devant Dieu ?
fr.R: Oui, je sais que c’est vrai. \q Mais comment un être humain pourrait-il gagner un procès contre Dieu ?

sw.L: Kweli najua kwamba [ni] hivyo; \q na mwanadamu awezaje kuwa na haki mbele za Mungu?
sw.B: Ndiyo, najua kwamba ni hivyo; \q lakini mwanadamu awezaje kuonekana hana hatia mbele za Mungu?
sw.R: Ndiyo, najua hili ni kweli. \q Lakini binadamu yeyote awezaje kushinda kesi dhidi ya Mungu?

vi.L: Thật, tôi biết rằng [điều ấy là] như vậy; \q và làm sao một người phàm được xem là đúng trước Đức Chúa Trời?
vi.B: Phải, tôi biết điều đó đúng như vậy; \q nhưng làm sao một người phàm được xử là đúng trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời?
vi.R: Phải, tôi biết điều ấy là thật. \q Nhưng làm sao một con người thắng kiện được Đức Chúa Trời?

ko.L: 참으로 그러한 줄 내가 안다. \q 사람이 어찌 하나님과 더불어 옳을 수 있겠느냐?
ko.B: 그렇다, 그것이 그러한 줄 나도 안다. \q 그러나 사람이 어떻게 하나님 앞에서 옳다고 인정받을 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 그렇다, 그 말이 맞다는 것은 나도 안다. \q 그러나 사람이 어떻게 하나님을 상대로 재판에서 이길 수 있겠느냐?

decisions.choice: it is so: Job grants what the friends have said
decisions.reason: Job begins by agreeing in part. Bildad said God does not twist justice (8:3), and Eliphaz asked whether a mortal can be right before God (4:17). Job grants the point, then turns it: the problem is not that God is unjust in a simple way, but that no human can stand up to him in a hearing.

decisions.choice: be in the right: win one's case, be declared innocent
decisions.reason: The verb (tsadaq) here is a word of the law court: to be in the right, to be found innocent in a dispute (13:18; Isaiah 43:9, 26). The next verse goes on with a lawsuit, so the question is not how a person becomes good but how anyone could win a case against God.

decisions.choice: a mortal: a frail human being
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) stresses human weakness and mortality (4:17; 7:1, 17). It means any person, not a man as opposed to a woman.

decisions.choice: God: the word 'El
decisions.reason: Job uses the short name for God, 'El, rendered "God" throughout Job.

decisions.choice: be in the right (B), win a case (R)
decisions.reason: "Be righteous" would suggest moral goodness; the sense here is winning a legal case (m2), which Balanced says with "be in the right" and Readable plainly.

decisions.choice: Job says "tôi" and speaks of God as "Ngài"
decisions.reason: Here Job speaks about God, not to him, so he says "tôi"; when he turns to God (9:28-31; chapter 10) he calls himself "con" and God "Chúa".

decisions.choice: the plain written style (해라체) with 나 for Job's reply in chapters 9 and 10
decisions.reason: Job does not address Bildad or the friends with "you" in this speech; he reflects aloud and then turns to God. His musing takes the plain style of a lament, as elsewhere in the book, and his words to God take 합쇼체 (9:28-31; chapter 10).

source.text: אִם־יַ֭חְפֹּץ לָרִ֣יב עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יַ֝עֲנֶ֗נּוּ אַחַ֥ת מִנִּי־אָֽלֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: If he wishes to contend with him, not he could answer him one from a thousand.

en.L: If one wished to contend with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q he could not answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} one [time] out of a thousand.
en.B: If someone wished to argue a case with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q they could not answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} once in a thousand times.
en.R: If someone wanted to take God to court, \q they could not answer one question in a thousand.

es.L: Si [uno] quisiera litigar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podría responder una [vez] de mil.
es.B: Si alguien quisiera entablar pleito con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podría responder ni una vez entre mil.
es.R: Si alguien quisiera llevar a Dios a juicio, \q no podría responder ni una pregunta de cada mil.

fr.L: Si [quelqu’un] voulait plaider contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q il ne pourrait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre une [fois] sur mille.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un voulait entrer en procès avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q il ne pourrait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre une seule fois sur mille.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un voulait traîner Dieu en justice, \q il ne pourrait pas répondre à une seule question sur mille.

sw.L: Ikiwa [mtu] angetaka kushindana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, \q hangeweza kumjibu mara moja kati ya elfu.
sw.B: Kama mtu angetaka kufungua kesi {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, \q hangeweza kumjibu hata mara moja kati ya elfu.
sw.R: Kama mtu angetaka kumpeleka Mungu mahakamani, \q hangeweza kujibu hata swali moja kati ya elfu.

vi.L: Nếu [ai] muốn tranh tụng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q người ấy không thể đáp lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một [lần] trong một ngàn.
vi.B: Nếu ai muốn kiện tụng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q người ấy không thể đáp lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dù chỉ một lần trong ngàn lần.
vi.R: Nếu có ai muốn kiện Đức Chúa Trời ra tòa, \q người ấy không trả lời nổi một câu trong một ngàn câu hỏi.

ko.L: [누가] 그분과 논쟁하기를 원한다 해도, \q 천 [번]에 한 번도 그분께 대답하지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 누가 그분과 소송을 벌이려 해도, \q 천 번에 한 번도 그분께 대답할 수 없을 것이다.
ko.R: 누가 하나님을 재판에 세우려 해도, \q 천 가지 질문 가운데 하나도 대답하지 못할 것이다.

decisions.choice: the person could not answer God
alternatives: God would not answer the person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "he" and "him": "if he wishes to contend with him, he will not answer him". It is most natural to read the person as the one who cannot answer, since God asks the questions in a hearing, as he will in 38:3 and 40:2. It could also mean that God would not answer even one of a person's thousand charges; both readings leave the human helpless.

decisions.choice: contend: argue a legal case
decisions.reason: The verb (riv) is used of bringing a lawsuit (10:2; 13:8; 23:6). Job pictures a trial with God, a picture he keeps through these chapters (9:14-20, 32-35; 10:2).

decisions.choice: one from a thousand: not even once
decisions.reason: "One out of a thousand" means almost never: of a thousand questions, he could not answer one.

decisions.choice: one (subject supplied); he and him
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the pronouns of the Hebrew, read as m1 takes them (he, the person; him, God), and supplies "one" for the unnamed subject.

decisions.choice: someone ... they (B, R); God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the person as "someone" and use "they" so the pronouns do not mix up the person and God; Readable names God.

source.text: חֲכַ֣ם לֵ֭בָב וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֑חַ מִֽי־הִקְשָׁ֥ה אֵ֝לָ֗יו וַיִּשְׁלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Wise of heart and mighty of strength: who has hardened [himself] against him and been whole?

en.L: Wise of heart and mighty in strength, \q who has hardened [himself] against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and stayed whole?
en.B: He is wise in heart and mighty in strength; \q who has ever defied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and come away unharmed?
en.R: God is wise and very powerful. \q No one has ever fought against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and come out unhurt.

es.L: Sabio de corazón y poderoso en fuerza, \q ¿quién se ha endurecido contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y ha quedado ileso?
es.B: Él es sabio de corazón y poderoso en fuerza; \q ¿quién {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha desafiado alguna vez y ha salido sin daño?
es.R: Dios es sabio y muy poderoso. \q Nadie se ha enfrentado jamás a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y ha salido sin daño.

fr.L: Sage de cœur et puissant en force, \q qui s’est endurci contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et est resté sain et sauf ?
fr.B: Il est sage de cœur et puissant en force ; \q qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a jamais défié et s’en est tiré indemne ?
fr.R: Dieu est sage et très puissant. \q Personne ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a jamais combattu et n’en est sorti indemne.

sw.L: Mwenye hekima moyoni na mwenye nguvu nyingi, \q ni nani aliyejifanya mgumu dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akabaki salama?
sw.B: Yeye ni mwenye hekima moyoni na mwenye nguvu nyingi; \q ni nani aliyewahi kumkaidi akatoka bila kudhurika?
sw.R: Mungu ana hekima na nguvu nyingi sana. \q Hakuna aliyewahi kupigana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akatoka salama.

vi.L: Khôn ngoan trong lòng và mạnh mẽ về sức lực, \q ai đã cứng cỏi chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà vẫn được nguyên vẹn?
vi.B: Ngài khôn ngoan trong lòng và quyền năng mạnh mẽ; \q có ai từng chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà vẫn bình an vô sự?
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời khôn ngoan và rất quyền năng. \q Chưa ai từng chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thoát khỏi tổn hại.

ko.L: 마음이 지혜롭고 힘이 강하신 분, \q 누가 그분께 고집을 부리고도 온전하였느냐?
ko.B: 그분은 마음이 지혜로우시고 힘이 강하신 분이다. \q 누가 그분께 맞서고도 무사하였느냐?
ko.R: 하나님은 지혜로우시고 아주 강하시다. \q 그분께 맞서 싸우고도 다치지 않은 사람은 아무도 없다.

decisions.choice: wise ... mighty: said of God
alternatives: said of the person who argues with God
decisions.reason: The first line has no verb or subject. It describes God, whose wisdom and power the next verses praise (9:5-10; 12:13); a person wise and strong would still lose to him, so the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: hardened himself against: stubbornly resisted
decisions.reason: The verb means "make hard", in full "harden the neck" (Deuteronomy 10:16; 2 Kings 17:14): to stand against someone stubbornly. Here it means to defy God.

decisions.choice: been whole: come through safe
decisions.reason: The verb (shalam) means to be whole or sound, to come through unharmed.

decisions.choice: He is
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies the subject and verb the Hebrew leaves out (m1). It is sentence-initial, so it is capitalized either way.

source.text: הַמַּעְתִּ֣יק הָ֭רִים וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עוּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הֲפָכָ֣ם בְּאַפּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: The one moving mountains and not they know, who overturns them in his anger;

en.L: [It is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] who moves mountains, and they do not know [it], \q who overturns them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger;
en.B: He moves mountains before they know it, \q and overturns them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger.
en.R: God moves mountains without warning. \q He turns them upside down when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is angry.

es.L: [Es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}] quien mueve las montañas, y ellas no [lo] saben, \q quien las trastorna en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira;
es.B: Mueve las montañas antes de que se den cuenta, \q y las vuelca en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira.
es.R: Dios mueve las montañas sin aviso. \q Las pone patas arriba cuando se enoja.

fr.L: [C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] qui déplace les montagnes, et elles ne [le] savent pas, \q qui les renverse dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ;
fr.B: Il déplace les montagnes avant qu’elles s’en aperçoivent, \q et les renverse dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère.
fr.R: Dieu déplace les montagnes sans prévenir. \q Il les met sens dessus dessous quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est en colère.

sw.L: [Ni {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}] aiondoaye milima, nayo haijui, \q aipinduaye katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}};
sw.B: Huihamisha milima kabla haijatambua, \q na kuipindua katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Mungu huihamisha milima bila onyo. \q Huipindua juu chini anapokasirika.

vi.L: [Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] là Đấng dời núi mà núi không hay biết, \q Đấng lật đổ chúng trong cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}};
vi.B: Ngài dời núi trước khi núi kịp hay biết, \q và lật đổ chúng trong cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời dời núi mà không báo trước. \q Khi nổi giận, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lật ngược chúng lên.

ko.L: 산들을 옮기시되 그것들이 알지 못하고, \q 진노하셔서 그것들을 뒤엎으시는 분,
ko.B: 그분은 산들이 알아차리기도 전에 옮기시고 \q 진노하셔서 그것들을 뒤엎으신다.
ko.R: 하나님은 아무 예고 없이 산을 옮기신다. \q 화가 나시면 산을 뒤집어엎으신다.

decisions.choice: a hymn of God's deeds
decisions.reason: Verses 5-10 describe God with a string of "the one who ..." phrases, the style of a hymn (compare 5:9-16; Amos 4:13; 5:8). Job praises God's power, but in this setting the praise frightens him: such power is used in anger (verses 5, 13).

decisions.choice: they do not know: suddenly, before the mountains are aware
decisions.reason: "And they do not know" most likely has the mountains as subject: they are moved before they know it, that is, all at once. It may also mean that no one knows it has happened.

decisions.choice: before they know it
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the sense of the Hebrew (m2) into an English phrase for something sudden.

decisions.choice: without warning
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "they do not know" means (m2).

source.text: הַמַּרְגִּ֣יז אֶ֭רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ וְ֝עַמּוּדֶ֗יהָ יִתְפַלָּצֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: The one shaking earth from its place, and its pillars shudder;

en.L: who shakes [the] earth from its place, \q and its pillars shudder;
en.B: He shakes the earth out of its place, \q and its pillars tremble.
en.R: He shakes the earth from where it stands, \q and the pillars under it shake.

es.L: quien sacude [la] tierra de su lugar, \q y sus columnas se estremecen;
es.B: Sacude la tierra y la saca de su lugar, \q y sus columnas tiemblan.
es.R: Sacude la tierra desde donde está, \q y los pilares que la sostienen se estremecen.

fr.L: qui secoue [la] terre hors de sa place, \q et ses colonnes frémissent ;
fr.B: Il ébranle la terre hors de sa place, \q et ses colonnes tremblent.
fr.R: Il secoue la terre là où elle se trouve, \q et les piliers qui la portent tremblent.

sw.L: aitikisaye nchi itoke mahali pake, \q na nguzo zake zinatetemeka;
sw.B: Huitikisa dunia itoke mahali pake, \q na nguzo zake zinatetemeka.
sw.R: Huitikisa dunia mahali ilipo, \q na nguzo zilizo chini yake zinatikisika.

vi.L: Đấng làm rung chuyển đất khỏi chỗ của nó, \q và các cột trụ của nó run rẩy;
vi.B: Ngài làm rung chuyển trái đất khỏi chỗ của nó, \q và các cột trụ của nó run lên.
vi.R: Ngài làm trái đất rung chuyển tại chỗ, \q và các cột trụ bên dưới cũng lung lay.

ko.L: 땅을 그 자리에서 흔드시니 \q 그 기둥들이 떤다.
ko.B: 그분은 땅을 그 자리에서 뒤흔드시니 \q 땅의 기둥들이 떤다.
ko.R: 그분이 땅을 그 자리에서 흔드시면 \q 땅을 받치는 기둥들이 흔들린다.

decisions.choice: the pillars of the earth: a picture of the world's foundations
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry pictures the earth as set on pillars or foundations that God holds firm or shakes (1 Samuel 2:8; Psalm 75:4; Job 38:4-6). The picture is of God's power over what seems most solid.

decisions.choice: shudder: shake, tremble
decisions.reason: The verb (palats) is a rare word for shaking or trembling with fear, used again of the pillars of heaven in 26:11.

source.text: הָאֹמֵ֣ר לַ֭חֶרֶס וְלֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ח וּבְעַ֖ד כּוֹכָבִ֣ים יַחְתֹּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The one speaking to the sun, and not it rises; and behind the stars he puts a seal;

en.L: who speaks to the sun, and it does not rise, \q and seals up behind the stars;
en.B: He speaks to the sun, and it does not rise; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts the stars under seal.
en.R: He can tell the sun not to rise. \q He can lock the stars away so they do not shine.

es.L: quien habla al sol, y no sale, \q y pone sello detrás de las estrellas;
es.B: Habla al sol, y este no sale; \q pone bajo sello las estrellas.
es.R: Puede ordenarle al sol que no salga. \q Puede encerrar las estrellas para que no brillen.

fr.L: qui parle au soleil, et il ne se lève pas, \q et qui met un sceau derrière les étoiles ;
fr.B: Il parle au soleil, et le soleil ne se lève pas ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} met les étoiles sous scellés.
fr.R: Il peut dire au soleil de ne pas se lever. \q Il peut enfermer les étoiles pour qu’elles ne brillent plus.

sw.L: aliambiaye jua, nalo halichomozi, \q na kutia muhuri nyuma ya nyota;
sw.B: Huliambia jua, nalo halichomozi; \q huzitia nyota muhuri.
sw.R: Anaweza kuliambia jua lisichomoze. \q Anaweza kuzifungia nyota ili zisiangaze.

vi.L: Đấng phán với mặt trời, và nó không mọc, \q và niêm phong phía sau các vì sao;
vi.B: Ngài phán với mặt trời, và nó không mọc lên; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} niêm phong các vì sao.
vi.R: Ngài có thể bảo mặt trời đừng mọc. \q Ngài có thể khóa các vì sao lại để chúng không chiếu sáng.

ko.L: 해에게 말씀하시니 떠오르지 않고, \q 별들 뒤에 봉인을 치신다.
ko.B: 그분께서 해에게 말씀하시면 해가 떠오르지 않고, \q 별들을 봉인하여 가두신다.
ko.R: 그분은 해에게 뜨지 말라고 하실 수 있다. \q 별들을 가두어 빛나지 못하게 하실 수 있다.

decisions.choice: the sun: a rare poetic word
decisions.reason: The word (cheres) is a rare name for the sun (Judges 8:13; 14:18), not the usual one.

decisions.choice: seals up behind the stars: shuts them away so they do not shine
decisions.reason: A seal closed up a document or a store so that no one could open it. God can shut the stars away like something sealed, so the night sky is dark. Compare 37:7, where he seals up the hand of every person.

decisions.choice: so they do not shine
decisions.reason: Readable says what sealing up the stars means (m2).

source.text: נֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַ֣יִם לְבַדּ֑וֹ וְ֝דוֹרֵ֗ךְ עַל־בָּ֥מֳתֵי יָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Stretching out heavens by himself, and treading on [the] heights of [the] sea;

en.L: who stretches out [the] heavens by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} \q and treads on [the] heights of [the] sea;
en.B: By {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stretched out the heavens, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} treads on the waves of the sea.
en.R: God alone spread out the sky. \q He walks on the high waves of the sea.

es.L: quien extiende [los] cielos {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} solo \q y pisa sobre [las] alturas del mar;
es.B: Él solo extendió los cielos, \q y camina sobre las olas del mar.
es.R: Solo Dios extendió el cielo. \q Camina sobre las altas olas del mar.

fr.L: qui étend [les] cieux à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} seul \q et marche sur [les] hauteurs de [la] mer ;
fr.B: À {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} seul, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a déployé les cieux, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} marche sur les vagues de la mer.
fr.R: Dieu seul a étendu le ciel. \q Il marche sur les hautes vagues de la mer.

sw.L: azitandaye mbingu peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} \q na kukanyaga juu ya vilele vya bahari;
sw.B: Peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} alizitandaza mbingu, \q na hukanyaga mawimbi ya bahari.
sw.R: Mungu peke yake alizitandaza mbingu. \q Hutembea juu ya mawimbi makubwa ya bahari.

vi.L: Đấng một mình giương các tầng trời ra \q và đạp trên [các] đỉnh cao của biển;
vi.B: Một mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã giăng các tầng trời ra, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bước đi trên sóng biển.
vi.R: Chỉ một mình Đức Chúa Trời trải rộng bầu trời. \q Ngài bước đi trên những ngọn sóng cao của biển.

ko.L: 홀로 하늘을 펴시고 \q 바다의 높은 곳을 밟으시는 분,
ko.B: 그분은 홀로 하늘을 펼치셨고 \q 바다의 파도를 밟고 다니신다.
ko.R: 하나님 혼자서 하늘을 펼치셨다. \q 그분은 바다의 높은 파도 위를 걸으신다.

decisions.choice: by himself: alone, with no one's help
decisions.reason: The phrase means God did it alone (Isaiah 44:24, "who stretched out the heavens alone").

decisions.choice: the heights of the sea: the high waves, and the sea as a power God tramples
alternatives: the back of the sea monster
decisions.reason: The word (bamot) means high places or backs. To tread on the heights or back of something is to master it (Deuteronomy 33:29; Amos 4:13). In the old poems the Sea is a wild power that God subdues (7:12; 26:12; 38:8-11), so the line pictures God walking on the waves as their master.

decisions.choice: the waves of the sea
decisions.reason: Balanced names the heights of the sea as its waves, which keeps the picture readable in English; the further sense of mastering the Sea is in the meaning decision (m2).

source.text: עֹֽשֶׂה־עָ֭שׁ כְּסִ֥יל וְכִימָ֗ה וְחַדְרֵ֥י תֵמָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Making [the] Bear, Orion and [the] Pleiades, and [the] chambers of [the] south;

en.L: who makes [the] Bear, Orion and [the] Pleiades, \q and [the] chambers of [the] south;
en.B: He made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades, \q and the star clusters of the south.
en.R: He made the groups of stars: the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades, \q and the stars in the southern sky.

es.L: quien hace [la] Osa, Orión y [las] Pléyades, \q y [las] cámaras del sur;
es.B: Él hizo la Osa y Orión, las Pléyades \q y las constelaciones del sur.
es.R: Él hizo los grupos de estrellas: la Osa, Orión y las Pléyades, \q y las estrellas del cielo del sur.

fr.L: qui fait l’Ourse, Orion et les Pléiades, \q et les chambres du midi ;
fr.B: Il a fait l’Ourse et Orion, les Pléiades \q et les amas d’étoiles du sud.
fr.R: Il a fait les groupes d’étoiles : l’Ourse, Orion et les Pléiades, \q et les étoiles du ciel du sud.

sw.L: afanyaye Dubu, Orioni na Kilimia, \q na vyumba vya kusini;
sw.B: Aliumba Dubu na Orioni, Kilimia, \q na makundi ya nyota ya kusini.
sw.R: Aliumba makundi ya nyota: Dubu, Orioni na Kilimia, \q na nyota za anga la kusini.

vi.L: Đấng làm nên sao Bắc Đẩu, sao Thần Nông và sao Rua, \q và [các] phòng của phương nam;
vi.B: Ngài dựng nên sao Bắc Đẩu và sao Thần Nông, sao Rua, \q và các chòm sao phương nam.
vi.R: Ngài dựng nên các chòm sao: sao Bắc Đẩu, sao Thần Nông và sao Rua, \q và những vì sao ở bầu trời phương nam.

ko.L: 북두성과 삼성과 묘성, \q 남쪽 하늘의 방들을 지으시는 분,
ko.B: 그분은 북두성과 삼성과 묘성을 지으시고 \q 남쪽 하늘의 별자리들도 지으셨다.
ko.R: 그분은 별자리들, 곧 북두성과 삼성과 묘성을 만드시고 \q 남쪽 하늘의 별들도 만드셨다.

decisions.choice: the Bear, Orion, the Pleiades: likely but not certain names of star groups
decisions.reason: The three Hebrew names ('Ash, Kesil and Kimah) are names of stars or constellations; they appear together again in 38:31-32 and Amos 5:8. Kimah, "cluster", is most likely the Pleiades, and Kesil, "fool", most likely Orion, the giant bound in the sky (38:31). 'Ash (spelled 'Ayish in 38:32) is the least certain; the Bear (the Big Dipper) is the usual identification, and others have been proposed. The point is that God made every star in the sky.

decisions.choice: the chambers of the south: the stars of the southern sky
alternatives: the storerooms of the south wind
decisions.reason: "Chambers" are inner rooms. Beside the names of constellations, "the chambers of the south" most likely means the star groups low in the southern sky, or the parts of the sky hidden from view. Some take it as the storerooms from which the south wind comes (37:9).

decisions.choice: the star clusters of the south
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the "chambers" most likely are (m2) rather than keep a picture that would puzzle English readers; Literal keeps "chambers".

decisions.choice: the groups of stars
decisions.reason: Readable says these are constellations, since the names alone may not tell the reader.

decisions.choice: "sao Bắc Đẩu, sao Thần Nông, sao Rua"
alternatives: chòm Gấu, chòm Lạp Hộ, chòm Thất Tinh
decisions.reason: The traditional Vietnamese names of the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades, used for the same three names in 38:31-32; which stars the Hebrew names meant is not certain (m1).

decisions.choice: 북두성, 삼성, 묘성
decisions.reason: The traditional East Asian names of the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades, kept for 38:31-32 as well; the modern astronomical names are the alternative. Which stars the Hebrew names meant is not certain (m1).

source.text: עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת עַד־אֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר וְנִפְלָא֗וֹת עַד־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Doing great [things] until there is no searching, and wonders until there is no number.

en.L: who does great [things] beyond searching out, \q and wonders beyond number.
en.B: He does great things too deep to search out, \q and wonders too many to count.
en.R: He does great things that no one can understand, \q and amazing things that no one can count.

es.L: quien hace cosas grandes hasta [no haber] escudriñarlas, \q y maravillas hasta [no haber] número.
es.B: Hace cosas grandes e insondables, \q y maravillas que no se pueden contar.
es.R: Hace cosas grandes que nadie puede entender, \q y cosas maravillosas que nadie puede contar.

fr.L: qui fait de grandes choses jusqu’à [n’avoir] pas [moyen de les] sonder, \q et des merveilles jusqu’à [n’avoir] pas de nombre.
fr.B: Il fait de grandes choses, insondables, \q et des merveilles qu’on ne peut compter.
fr.R: Il fait de grandes choses que personne ne peut comprendre, \q et des merveilles que personne ne peut compter.

sw.L: afanyaye mambo makuu hata [hakuna] kuyachunguza, \q na maajabu hata [hakuna] hesabu.
sw.B: Hufanya mambo makuu yasiyochunguzika, \q na maajabu yasiyoweza kuhesabika.
sw.R: Hufanya mambo makuu ambayo hakuna mtu awezaye kuyaelewa, \q na maajabu ambayo hakuna mtu awezaye kuyahesabu.

vi.L: Đấng làm những việc lớn lao đến [không thể] dò thấu, \q và những việc diệu kỳ đến [không thể] đếm được.
vi.B: Ngài làm những việc lớn lao không thể dò thấu, \q và những việc diệu kỳ không sao đếm xuể.
vi.R: Ngài làm những việc lớn lao không ai hiểu nổi, \q và những việc kỳ diệu không ai đếm được.

ko.L: 큰일들을 행하시되 측량할 수 없고, \q 기이한 일들을 행하시되 셀 수 없다.
ko.B: 그분은 헤아릴 수 없는 큰일을 하시고 \q 셀 수 없이 많은 기이한 일을 하신다.
ko.R: 그분은 아무도 이해할 수 없는 큰일을 하시고, \q 아무도 셀 수 없는 놀라운 일을 하신다.

decisions.choice: Job repeats Eliphaz's words
decisions.reason: This verse is almost word for word what Eliphaz said in 5:9. Eliphaz used it to urge Job to seek God; Job uses the same praise to say that this great God cannot be faced in a hearing (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: until there is no searching: beyond finding out
decisions.reason: "Until there is no searching" means past the point where anyone could search it out (Psalm 145:3; Isaiah 40:28).

decisions.choice: the wording of 5:9
decisions.reason: Job repeats Eliphaz's words of 5:9 almost exactly (m1), so the Spanish of 5:9 is reused; only the "and" the Hebrew adds here is new.

decisions.choice: the wording of 5:9
decisions.reason: Job repeats Eliphaz's words of 5:9 almost exactly (m1), so the French of 5:9 is reused; only the "and" the Hebrew adds here is new.

decisions.choice: the wording of 5:9
decisions.reason: Job repeats Eliphaz's words of 5:9 almost exactly (m1), so the Swahili of 5:9 is reused; only the "and" the Hebrew adds here is new.

decisions.choice: the wording of 5:9
decisions.reason: Job repeats Eliphaz's words of 5:9 almost exactly (m1), so the Vietnamese of 5:9 is reused; only the "and" the Hebrew adds here is new.

decisions.choice: the wording of 5:9, in Job's plain style
decisions.reason: Job repeats Eliphaz's words of 5:9 almost exactly (m1), so the Korean of 5:9 is reused, with Job's plain endings (셀 수 없다) in place of Eliphaz's 하오체.

source.text: הֵ֤ן יַעֲבֹ֣ר עָ֭לַי וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶ֑ה וְ֝יַחֲלֹ֗ף וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, he passes by me and not I see [him]; and he moves on, and not I perceive him.

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passes by me, and I do not see [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moves on, and I do not perceive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passes by me, I do not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moves on, I cannot perceive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: God may go right past me, but I do not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q He moves on, and I do not even notice {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Mira, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pasa junto a mí, y no [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] veo; \q pasa de largo, y no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} percibo.
es.B: Si pasa junto a mí, no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veo; \q si sigue de largo, no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} percibo.
es.R: Dios puede pasar justo a mi lado, pero no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veo. \q Sigue su camino, y ni siquiera {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} noto.

fr.L: Voici, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passe près de moi, et je ne [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] vois pas ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’en va, et je ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} discerne pas.
fr.B: S’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passe près de moi, je ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} vois pas ; \q s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’éloigne, je ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aperçois pas.
fr.R: Dieu peut passer tout près de moi sans que je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voie. \q Il continue son chemin, et je ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} remarque même pas.

sw.L: Tazama, ananipita, wala simwoni; \q anaendelea mbele, wala simtambui.
sw.B: Akinipita, simwoni; \q akiendelea mbele, simtambui.
sw.R: Mungu anaweza kupita karibu nami, lakini simwoni. \q Anaendelea na safari yake, wala simtambui hata kidogo.

vi.L: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ngang qua tôi, mà tôi không thấy [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}]; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi tiếp, mà tôi không nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ngang qua tôi, tôi không thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi tiếp, tôi cũng không nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời có thể đi ngay bên cạnh tôi, nhưng tôi không thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Ngài đi tiếp, và tôi cũng chẳng hay biết.

ko.L: 보라, 그분께서 내 곁을 지나가셔도 나는 [그분을] 보지 못하고, \q 그분께서 지나쳐 가셔도 나는 그분을 알아차리지 못한다.
ko.B: 그분께서 내 곁을 지나가셔도 나는 그분을 보지 못하고, \q 그분께서 지나쳐 가셔도 나는 알아차리지 못한다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 바로 내 곁을 지나가셔도 나는 그분을 보지 못한다. \q 그분이 지나가셔도 나는 눈치채지도 못한다.

decisions.choice: look: a supposition, "suppose he passes by"
decisions.reason: The word (hen) points to something; here and in verse 12 it puts a case: should he pass by me ... The verbs speak of what may happen at any time.

decisions.choice: passes by ... moves on: the words of Eliphaz's night vision
decisions.reason: The two verbs echo 4:15, where a spirit "moved on" past Eliphaz's face. Eliphaz claimed a vision; Job says that when God passes by he cannot even see him (compare 23:8-9).

decisions.choice: If ... if
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the supposition in "look" (m1) with "if".

source.text: הֵ֣ן יַ֭חְתֹּף מִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ מִֽי־יֹאמַ֥ר אֵ֝לָ֗יו מַֽה־תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, he snatches away; who can turn him back? Who will say to him, What are you doing?

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} snatches away; who can turn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back? \q Who will say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} doing?"
en.B: If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} snatches something away, who can stop {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? \q Who can say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} doing?"
en.R: If God takes something away, no one can stop {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q No one can ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} doing?"

es.L: Mira, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} arrebata; ¿quién {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hará volver? \q ¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dirá: «¿Qué haces?»?
es.B: Si arrebata algo, ¿quién {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} detendrá? \q ¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} puede decir: «¿Qué haces?»?
es.R: Si Dios quita algo, nadie {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puede detener. \q Nadie {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} puede preguntar: «¿Qué estás haciendo?».

fr.L: Voici, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ravit ; qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fera revenir ? \q Qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dira : « Que fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »
fr.B: S’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enlève quelque chose, qui peut {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}arrêter ? \q Qui peut {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dire : « Que fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »
fr.R: Si Dieu prend quelque chose, personne ne peut {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}en empêcher. \q Personne ne peut {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander : « Qu’est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais ? »

sw.L: Tazama, ananyakua; ni nani atakayemrudisha? \q Ni nani atakayemwambia, “Unafanya nini?”
sw.B: Akinyakua kitu, ni nani awezaye kumzuia? \q Ni nani awezaye kumwambia, “Unafanya nini?”
sw.R: Mungu akichukua kitu, hakuna awezaye kumzuia. \q Hakuna awezaye kumwuliza, “Unafanya nini?”

vi.L: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chộp lấy; ai có thể bắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lại? \q Ai sẽ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: “Ngài làm gì vậy?”
vi.B: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cướp lấy điều gì, ai ngăn được {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}? \q Ai dám hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: “Ngài đang làm gì vậy?”
vi.R: Nếu Đức Chúa Trời lấy đi điều gì, không ai cản được {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Không ai có thể hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: “Ngài đang làm gì thế?”

ko.L: 보라, 그분께서 낚아채시니 누가 그분을 돌이키겠느냐? \q 누가 그분께 “무엇을 하십니까?” 하고 말하겠느냐?
ko.B: 그분께서 무엇을 빼앗아 가셔도 누가 막을 수 있겠느냐? \q 누가 그분께 “무엇을 하시는 겁니까?” 하고 따질 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 하나님께서 무엇을 가져가셔도 아무도 막을 수 없다. \q 아무도 그분께 “지금 무엇을 하시는 겁니까?” 하고 물을 수 없다.

decisions.choice: snatches away: seizes suddenly, as prey
decisions.reason: The verb (chataf) is used of a robber or wild animal seizing prey (Proverbs 23:28). Job has had everything taken from him (1:21, "the one who gave has taken away").

decisions.choice: Who will say to him, What are you doing?: no one can call God to account
decisions.reason: The same question is asked of a king whose word no one can question (Ecclesiastes 8:4). Job's complaint is that God is answerable to no one.

decisions.choice: no one can ... (statements)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into the statements they imply, "no one can".

source.text: אֱ֭לוֹהַּ לֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ תַּחְתָּ֥יו שָׁ֝חֲח֗וּ עֹ֣זְרֵי רָֽהַב׃

records.literal_gloss: God not will turn back his anger; under him bowed down [the] helpers of Rahab.

en.L: God will not turn back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger; \q under {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} bowed down [the] helpers of Rahab.
en.B: God does not hold back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger; \q the helpers of Rahab bowed down beneath {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: God does not hold back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. \q Even the helpers of Rahab, the sea monster, fell down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Dios no retirará {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira; \q bajo {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se postraron [los] ayudantes de Rahab.
es.B: Dios no contiene {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira; \q los ayudantes de Rahab se doblegaron bajo {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Dios no detiene {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enojo. \q Hasta los ayudantes de Rahab, el monstruo del mar, cayeron rendidos delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Dieu ne retirera pas {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ; \q sous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} se sont courbés [les] auxiliaires de Rahab.
fr.B: Dieu ne retient pas {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ; \q les alliés de Rahab se sont courbés sous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Dieu ne retient pas {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère. \q Même les alliés de Rahab, le monstre de la mer, sont tombés à terre devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Mungu hataizuia hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}; \q chini {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} wasaidizi wa Rahabu walisujudu.
sw.B: Mungu haizuii hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}; \q wasaidizi wa Rahabu walisalimu amri chini {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Mungu haizuii hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Hata wasaidizi wa Rahabu, yule mnyama mkubwa wa baharini, walianguka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời không rút lại cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q dưới {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [những] kẻ giúp Ra-háp đã cúi rạp.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời không kìm cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q những kẻ trợ giúp Ra-háp đã phục xuống dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời không nén cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Ngay cả những kẻ giúp Ra-háp, con quái vật biển, cũng phải ngã rạp trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 하나님께서 그분의 진노를 거두지 않으시니, \q 라합을 돕는 자들이 그분 아래 엎드렸다.
ko.B: 하나님은 진노를 거두지 않으신다. \q 라합을 돕는 자들도 그분 발아래 굴복하였다.
ko.R: 하나님은 화를 참지 않으신다. \q 바다 괴물 라합을 돕던 자들조차 그분 앞에 엎드러졌다.

decisions.choice: God: the word 'Eloah
decisions.reason: Job uses 'Eloah, a name for God common in Job, rendered "God".

decisions.choice: Rahab: the sea monster of chaos in the old poems, not Rahab of Jericho
decisions.reason: Rahab (rahav, "storming" or "arrogant one") is the name of a monster of the sea that God defeated, a picture of the forces of chaos he holds in check (26:12; Psalm 89:11; Isaiah 51:9). It is spelled differently in Hebrew from the name of Rahab of Jericho (Joshua 2:1), who has nothing to do with it. Elsewhere the name is used as a poetic name for Egypt (Isaiah 30:7; Psalm 87:4). Rahab's "helpers" are the powers that sided with the monster; if even they lay flat beneath God, Job cannot stand before him. The name stays "Rahab" at every level.

decisions.choice: not turn back his anger: not hold back, not relent
decisions.reason: To "turn back" anger is to withdraw it (Psalm 78:38). God's anger, once roused, is not called off.

decisions.choice: bowed down: lay flat in defeat
decisions.reason: The verb (shachach) means to stoop or lie low; here it is the posture of the defeated lying under the victor (the same verb in Isaiah 2:11 of the proud brought low).

decisions.choice: the sea monster
decisions.reason: Readable adds who Rahab is (m2), so the reader does not think of Rahab of Jericho.

source.text: אַ֭ף כִּֽי־אָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ אֶבְחֲרָ֖ה דְבָרַ֣י עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: How much less I, [how] could I answer him, choose my words with him?

en.L: How much less I, [how] could I answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q choose my words with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.B: How then could I answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q or choose my words to argue with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.R: So how could I ever answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? \q How could I find the right words to argue with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?

es.L: ¿Cuánto menos yo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podría responder, \q escoger mis palabras frente a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}?
es.B: ¿Cómo, entonces, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podría responder yo, \q o escoger mis palabras para discutir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}?
es.R: Entonces, ¿cómo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podría responder yo? \q ¿Cómo encontraría las palabras justas para discutir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}?

fr.L: Combien moins moi, [comment] {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondrais-je, \q choisirais-je mes paroles face à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ?
fr.B: Comment donc pourrais-je {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre, \q ou choisir mes mots pour plaider contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ?
fr.R: Alors comment pourrais-je {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre ? \q Comment trouverais-je les bons mots pour discuter avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ?

sw.L: Sembuse mimi, [nitawezaje] kumjibu, \q na kuchagua maneno yangu kwa kujibizana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}?
sw.B: Basi mimi ningewezaje kumjibu, \q au kuchagua maneno ya kushindana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}?
sw.R: Kwa hiyo ningewezaje kumjibu? \q Ningepataje maneno sahihi ya kubishana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}?

vi.L: Huống chi tôi, [làm sao] tôi đáp lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q lựa lời mình với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?
vi.B: Vậy làm sao tôi có thể đáp lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q hay chọn lời để tranh luận với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?
vi.R: Thế thì làm sao tôi trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi? \q Làm sao tôi tìm được lời lẽ thích hợp để tranh luận với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?

ko.L: 하물며 내가 어찌 그분께 대답하며, \q 그분 앞에서 내 말을 고르겠느냐?
ko.B: 그러니 내가 어떻게 그분께 대답하며, \q 그분과 따질 말을 고를 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 그러니 내가 어떻게 그분께 대답할 수 있겠느냐? \q 그분과 다툴 알맞은 말을 어떻게 찾겠느냐?

decisions.choice: how much less I: if Rahab's helpers fell, Job has no chance
decisions.reason: The words ('af ki) argue from the greater to the lesser: if the monster's helpers were brought low (verse 13), how much less can Job stand before God.

decisions.choice: choose my words: find arguments for a hearing
decisions.reason: To choose words is to pick out what to say in a legal case. Job pictures himself searching for words before a judge who is also his opponent.

decisions.choice: How then
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the argument (m1) with "how then", more natural in English than "how much less I".

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־צָ֭דַקְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶעֱנֶ֑ה לִ֝מְשֹׁפְטִ֗י אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Who, if I were in the right, not I would answer; to my judge I would plead for mercy.

en.L: I who, though I were in the right, could not answer; \q to my judge I would [have to] plead for mercy.
en.B: Even if I were in the right, I could not answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q I would have to beg my judge for mercy.
en.R: Even if I were innocent, I could not answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q All I could do is beg my judge to have mercy on me.

es.L: Yo, que aunque tuviera la razón, no podría responder; \q a mi juez [tendría que] suplicarle misericordia.
es.B: Aunque tuviera la razón, no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podría responder; \q tendría que rogar a mi juez que me tuviera compasión.
es.R: Aunque fuera inocente, no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podría responder. \q Lo único que podría hacer es rogar a mi juez que tenga compasión de mí.

fr.L: moi qui, même si j’étais dans mon droit, ne pourrais répondre ; \q à mon juge je [devrais] demander grâce.
fr.B: Même si j’étais dans mon droit, je ne pourrais pas {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre ; \q je devrais implorer la pitié de mon juge.
fr.R: Même si j’étais innocent, je ne pourrais pas {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre. \q Je pourrais seulement supplier mon juge d’avoir pitié de moi.

sw.L: mimi ambaye, hata kama ningekuwa na haki, nisingeweza kujibu; \q kwa mwamuzi wangu [ningelazimika] kuomba rehema.
sw.B: Hata kama ningekuwa na haki, nisingeweza kumjibu; \q ningelazimika kumsihi mwamuzi wangu anihurumie.
sw.R: Hata kama sina hatia, nisingeweza kumjibu. \q Ningeweza tu kumwomba mwamuzi wangu anionee huruma.

vi.L: Tôi là người, dù có lý, cũng không thể đáp lại; \q tôi [phải] nài xin ơn thương xót nơi Đấng xét xử tôi.
vi.B: Dù tôi có lý, tôi cũng không thể đáp lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q tôi phải van xin Đấng xét xử tôi thương xót.
vi.R: Dù tôi vô tội, tôi cũng không thể trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Tôi chỉ còn biết van xin Đấng xét xử tôi thương xót tôi.

ko.L: 내가 옳다 할지라도 대답하지 못하고, \q 나를 심판하시는 분께 은혜를 구해야 [할] 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 옳다 해도 그분께 대답할 수 없고, \q 나를 심판하시는 분께 자비를 빌어야 할 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 죄가 없다 해도 그분께 대답할 수 없다. \q 그저 나를 재판하시는 분께 불쌍히 여겨 달라고 빌 수밖에 없다.

decisions.choice: were in the right: were innocent in the case
decisions.reason: The verb (tsadaq) is the court word of verse 2: to have the right on one's side.

decisions.choice: my judge: the one who brings a case against me
decisions.reason: The form (meshofeti) is unusual; it means the one who judges me or who brings judgment against me, so it can mean either the judge or the opponent in the case. In Job's picture God is both, which is the heart of his trouble.

decisions.choice: plead for mercy: ask for a favor one has no right to
decisions.reason: The verb (chanan, in the reflexive form) means to beg for grace or pity. Even an innocent man would be reduced to begging, not arguing his case.

decisions.choice: him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who would not be answered, God, as the verses before do.

source.text: אִם־קָרָ֥אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑נִי לֹֽא־אַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּֽי־יַאֲזִ֥ין קוֹלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: If I called and he answered me, not I would believe that he was listening to my voice.

en.L: If I called and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me, \q I would not believe that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was listening to my voice.
en.B: If I called and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me, \q I would not believe that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was listening to me.
en.R: Even if I called to God in court and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me, \q I could not believe {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was really listening to me.

es.L: Si yo llamara y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me respondiera, \q no creería que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} escuchara mi voz.
es.B: Si yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llamara y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me respondiera, \q no creería que me estuviera escuchando.
es.R: Aunque llamara a Dios a juicio y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me respondiera, \q no podría creer que de verdad me estuviera escuchando.

fr.L: Si j’appelais et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me répondait, \q je ne croirais pas qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} écoute ma voix.
fr.B: Si je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}appelais et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me répondait, \q je ne croirais pas qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’écoute.
fr.R: Même si j’appelais Dieu au tribunal et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me répondait, \q je ne pourrais pas croire qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’écoute vraiment.

sw.L: Kama ningeita, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akanijibu, \q nisingeamini kwamba anaisikiliza sauti yangu.
sw.B: Kama ningemwita, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akanijibu, \q nisingeamini kwamba ananisikiliza.
sw.R: Hata kama ningemwita Mungu mahakamani, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akanijibu, \q nisingeweza kuamini kwamba ananisikiliza kweli.

vi.L: Nếu tôi kêu và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời tôi, \q tôi cũng không tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lắng tai nghe tiếng tôi.
vi.B: Nếu tôi kêu và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời, \q tôi cũng không tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang nghe tôi.
vi.R: Dù tôi có gọi Đức Chúa Trời ra tòa và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lời tôi, \q tôi cũng không tin là {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật sự lắng nghe tôi.

ko.L: 내가 부르고 그분께서 내게 대답하셨다 해도, \q 그분께서 내 목소리에 귀 기울이셨다고 나는 믿지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 불러서 그분께서 대답하신다 해도, \q 그분께서 내 말을 듣고 계신다고 믿지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 하나님을 재판정에 불러 그분께서 대답하신다 해도, \q 그분께서 정말 내 말을 들으신다고는 믿을 수 없을 것이다.

decisions.choice: called: summoned him to a hearing
decisions.reason: In the setting of a lawsuit, to call is to summon the other party to court (13:22). Job says that even if God came to the hearing, Job would not trust that he was taking his words seriously.

decisions.choice: listening to my voice: paying attention to what I say
decisions.reason: "Give ear to my voice" means to hear and heed someone's words.

decisions.choice: in court
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the calling is a summons to a hearing (m1).

source.text: אֲשֶׁר־בִּשְׂעָרָ֥ה יְשׁוּפֵ֑נִי וְהִרְבָּ֖ה פְצָעַ֣י חִנָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who with a storm crushes me, and multiplies my wounds without cause;

en.L: [He] who crushes me with a storm \q and multiplies my wounds without cause;
en.B: He would crush me with a storm \q and multiply my wounds for no reason.
en.R: He would strike me down with a storm \q and give me wound after wound for no reason.

es.L: [Él], que me aplasta con una tempestad \q y multiplica mis heridas sin causa;
es.B: Me aplastaría con una tempestad \q y multiplicaría mis heridas sin motivo.
es.R: Me derribaría con una tempestad \q y me daría herida tras herida sin razón.

fr.L: [lui] qui m’écrase par une tempête \q et multiplie mes blessures sans cause ;
fr.B: Il m’écraserait dans la tempête \q et multiplierait mes blessures sans raison.
fr.R: Il m’abattrait par une tempête \q et me blesserait encore et encore sans raison.

sw.L: [Yeye] anipondaye kwa dhoruba \q na kuzidisha majeraha yangu bila sababu;
sw.B: Angeniponda kwa dhoruba \q na kuzidisha majeraha yangu bila sababu.
sw.R: Angenipiga kwa dhoruba \q na kunijeruhi tena na tena bila sababu.

vi.L: [Ngài là Đấng] nghiền nát tôi bằng cơn bão \q và gia tăng thương tích tôi vô cớ;
vi.B: Ngài sẽ nghiền nát tôi trong cơn bão \q và gia tăng thương tích tôi vô cớ.
vi.R: Ngài sẽ quật ngã tôi bằng cơn bão \q và gây cho tôi hết vết thương này đến vết thương khác mà chẳng vì lý do gì.

ko.L: 그분은 폭풍으로 나를 짓밟으시고 \q 까닭 없이 내 상처를 더하신다.
ko.B: 그분은 폭풍으로 나를 짓누르시고 \q 이유 없이 내 상처를 늘리실 것이다.
ko.R: 그분은 폭풍으로 나를 쓰러뜨리시고 \q 아무 이유 없이 상처에 상처를 더하실 것이다.

decisions.choice: without cause: the word of the prologue
decisions.reason: The word (chinnam) is the one the Accuser used (1:9, "Does Job fear God for nothing?") and that God used of Job's suffering (2:3, "to destroy him without cause"). Job does not know what the reader knows, but he has named exactly what happened to him.

decisions.choice: a storm: the word for the storm God will speak from
decisions.reason: The word (se'arah) is a storm wind. God answers Job "out of the storm" with the same word (38:1; 40:6). The same consonants can be read as a word for "hair", so some read "he crushes me for a hair", that is, for a trifle; the Hebrew vowels give "storm".

decisions.choice: crushes: what God would do if Job came to court
decisions.reason: Verse 17 continues verse 16 ("who ..."): if God met Job in court, he would crush him rather than listen. The verbs describe what Job expects, drawn from what he has already suffered.

decisions.choice: would crush
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable continue the "if" of verse 16 (m3) with "would": this is what Job expects God would do in court.

decisions.choice: "tempestad" at every level
decisions.reason: The same word names the storm God speaks from in 38:1 and 40:6 (m2), where the book's settled Spanish is "la tempestad"; keeping it here lets the reader hear the link.

source.text: לֹֽא־יִ֭תְּנֵנִי הָשֵׁ֣ב רוּחִ֑י כִּ֥י יַ֝שְׂבִּעַ֗נִי מַמְּרֹרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Not he lets me bring back my breath, for he fills me with bitter [things].

en.L: He does not let me get back my breath, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fills me with bitter [things].
en.B: He would not let me catch my breath, \q but would fill me with bitterness.
en.R: He would not even give me time to breathe. \q He would fill my life with bitter pain.

es.L: No me deja recobrar el aliento, \q pues me sacia de amarguras.
es.B: No me dejaría recobrar el aliento, \q sino que me llenaría de amargura.
es.R: Ni siquiera me daría tiempo para respirar. \q Llenaría mi vida de un dolor amargo.

fr.L: Il ne me laisse pas reprendre mon souffle, \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me rassasie d’amertumes.
fr.B: Il ne me laisserait pas reprendre haleine, \q mais me remplirait d’amertume.
fr.R: Il ne me laisserait même pas le temps de respirer. \q Il remplirait ma vie d’une douleur amère.

sw.L: Haniachi nirudishe pumzi yangu, \q kwa maana hunishibisha mambo machungu.
sw.B: Asingeniacha nipumue, \q bali angenijaza uchungu.
sw.R: Asingenipa hata nafasi ya kupumua. \q Angeyajaza maisha yangu maumivu makali.

vi.L: Ngài không để tôi lấy lại hơi thở, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm tôi no ngấy những điều cay đắng.
vi.B: Ngài không để tôi kịp thở, \q nhưng làm tôi đầy dẫy cay đắng.
vi.R: Ngài chẳng cho tôi được thở. \q Ngài làm đời tôi đầy những nỗi đau cay đắng.

ko.L: 그분은 내가 숨을 돌리지 못하게 하시고, \q 쓴 것들로 나를 배불리신다.
ko.B: 그분은 내가 숨 돌릴 틈도 주지 않으시고 \q 쓰라림으로 나를 채우실 것이다.
ko.R: 그분은 내게 숨 쉴 틈도 주지 않으실 것이다. \q 내 삶을 쓰라린 고통으로 가득 채우실 것이다.

decisions.choice: bring back my breath: catch one's breath, have a moment's rest
decisions.reason: "Return my breath" (ruach) means to recover one's breath. Job has said God will not let him alone long enough to swallow his spit (7:19).

decisions.choice: fills me with bitter things: fills me to the full with suffering
decisions.reason: The verb means to give someone more than enough, to glut them; here it is with bitterness (compare Lamentations 3:15).

decisions.choice: would
decisions.reason: The verse continues the supposition of verses 16-17, so Balanced and Readable keep "would".

source.text: אִם־לְכֹ֣חַ אַמִּ֣יץ הִנֵּ֑ה וְאִם־לְ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט מִ֣י יוֹעִידֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: If of strength, [the] mighty [one], look! And if of justice, who will summon me?

en.L: If [it is a matter] of strength, look, [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the] mighty [one]! \q And if of justice: "Who will summon me?"
en.B: If it is a matter of strength, look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the mighty one! \q If it is a matter of justice, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Who can summon me?"
en.R: If it is a contest of strength, God is far stronger. \q If it is a matter of justice, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asks, "Who can call me into court?"

es.L: Si [se trata] de fuerza, ¡mira, [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el] poderoso! \q Y si de justicia: «¿Quién me citará?».
es.B: Si se trata de fuerza, ¡mira, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el poderoso! \q Si se trata de justicia, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dice: «¿Quién puede citarme?».
es.R: Si es una competencia de fuerza, Dios es mucho más fuerte. \q Si es cuestión de justicia, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pregunta: «¿Quién puede llevarme a juicio?».

fr.L: S’[il s’agit] de force, voici, [{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est le] puissant ! \q Et s’[il s’agit] de droit : « Qui me citera ? »
fr.B: S’il s’agit de force, voici, c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} le puissant ! \q S’il s’agit de justice, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Qui peut me citer en justice ? »
fr.R: Si c’est une question de force, Dieu est bien plus fort. \q Si c’est une question de justice, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} demande : « Qui peut me traîner au tribunal ? »

sw.L: Ikiwa [ni jambo] la nguvu, tazama, [{{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye] mwenye uweza! \q Na ikiwa ni la hukumu: “Ni nani atakayeniita?”
sw.B: Ikiwa ni jambo la nguvu, tazama, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye mwenye nguvu! \q Ikiwa ni jambo la haki, anasema, “Ni nani awezaye kuniita mahakamani?”
sw.R: Ikiwa ni mashindano ya nguvu, Mungu ana nguvu kupita wote. \q Ikiwa ni jambo la haki, anauliza, “Ni nani awezaye kunipeleka mahakamani?”

vi.L: Nếu [là chuyện] sức mạnh, kìa, [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Đấng] dũng mãnh! \q Còn nếu [là chuyện] công lý: “Ai sẽ đòi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra hầu tòa?”
vi.B: Nếu là chuyện sức mạnh, kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Đấng dũng mãnh! \q Nếu là chuyện công lý, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: “Ai có thể đòi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra tòa?”
vi.R: Nếu so sức mạnh, Đức Chúa Trời mạnh hơn rất nhiều. \q Nếu là chuyện công lý, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi: “Ai có thể kiện {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra tòa?”

ko.L: 힘으로 하자면, 보라, 그분은 강하신 분이다! \q 공의로 하자면, “누가 나를 소환하겠느냐?”
ko.B: 힘을 겨루자면, 보라, 그분은 강하신 분이다! \q 정의를 따지자면, 그분은 “누가 나를 법정에 불러낼 수 있느냐?” 하신다.
ko.R: 힘을 겨룬다면, 하나님이 훨씬 더 강하시다. \q 정의를 따진다면, 그분은 “누가 나를 재판에 부를 수 있느냐?” 하고 물으신다.

decisions.choice: who will summon me: God's own challenge, which Job quotes
alternatives: who will set a hearing for me?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "who will summon me?", the same words God speaks in Jeremiah 49:19 and 50:44: no one can call him to court. Job seems to put the challenge in God's mouth. A change of one letter gives "who will summon him?", which makes Job the speaker throughout; some ancient translations read so. The sense is the same: no court can make God appear.

decisions.choice: summon: appoint a time for a hearing
decisions.reason: The verb (ya'ad) means to fix a meeting or summon someone to appear at an appointed time, here in court.

decisions.choice: he says (B), he asks (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add who speaks the question, so the reader sees that "me" is God (m1). Literal marks it with quotation marks only.

decisions.choice: God's challenge quoted with "Ta" ("Ai ... đòi Ta ra tòa?")
decisions.reason: The question is God's own (m1), so God speaks of himself as "Ta", as he does elsewhere; it carries a deity_pronoun span mid-sentence, though the English "me" has none.

source.text: אִם־אֶ֭צְדָּק פִּ֣י יַרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי תָּֽם־אָ֝֗נִי וַֽיַּעְקְשֵֽׁנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: If I were in the right, my mouth would condemn me; blameless I [am], and it would declare me crooked.

en.L: Though I were in the right, my own mouth would condemn me; \q [though] I [am] blameless, it would declare me crooked.
en.B: Even if I were in the right, my own mouth would condemn me; \q though I am blameless, it would prove me crooked.
en.R: Even if I were innocent, my own words would make me look guilty. \q I am blameless, but they would make me look crooked.

es.L: Aunque yo tuviera la razón, mi propia boca me condenaría; \q [aunque] yo [soy] íntegro, me declararía perverso.
es.B: Aunque tuviera la razón, mi propia boca me condenaría; \q aunque soy íntegro, me haría pasar por perverso.
es.R: Aunque fuera inocente, mis propias palabras me harían parecer culpable. \q Soy íntegro, pero ellas me harían parecer un deshonesto.

fr.L: Même si j’étais dans mon droit, ma propre bouche me condamnerait ; \q [quoique] je [sois] intègre, elle me déclarerait pervers.
fr.B: Même si j’étais dans mon droit, ma propre bouche me condamnerait ; \q bien que je sois intègre, elle me ferait passer pour pervers.
fr.R: Même si j’étais innocent, mes propres paroles me feraient paraître coupable. \q Je suis intègre, mais elles me feraient passer pour malhonnête.

sw.L: Hata kama ningekuwa na haki, kinywa changu mwenyewe kingenihukumu; \q [ingawa] mimi [ni] mkamilifu, kingenitangaza kuwa mpotovu.
sw.B: Hata kama ningekuwa na haki, kinywa changu mwenyewe kingenihukumu; \q ingawa mimi ni mkamilifu, kingenionyesha kuwa mpotovu.
sw.R: Hata kama sina hatia, maneno yangu mwenyewe yangenifanya nionekane mwenye hatia. \q Mimi ni mkamilifu, lakini yangenifanya nionekane mdanganyifu.

vi.L: Dù tôi có lý, chính miệng tôi sẽ kết án tôi; \q [dù] tôi trọn vẹn, nó sẽ tuyên bố tôi là gian tà.
vi.B: Dù tôi có lý, chính miệng tôi sẽ kết tội tôi; \q dù tôi trọn vẹn, nó sẽ chứng minh tôi là kẻ gian tà.
vi.R: Dù tôi vô tội, chính lời tôi nói sẽ làm tôi trông như có tội. \q Tôi trọn vẹn, nhưng lời tôi sẽ làm tôi trông như kẻ gian dối.

ko.L: 내가 옳다 할지라도 내 입이 나를 정죄할 것이요, \q 내가 흠이 없다 [할지라도] 내 입이 나를 비뚤어진 자라 할 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 옳다 해도 내 입이 나를 정죄할 것이고, \q 내가 흠이 없어도 내 입이 나를 비뚤어진 자로 만들 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 죄가 없다 해도 내 말 때문에 죄인처럼 보일 것이다. \q 나는 흠이 없지만, 내 말 때문에 비뚤어진 사람처럼 보일 것이다.

decisions.choice: blameless: the word of 1:1
decisions.reason: Job uses the word (tam) the narrator and God used of him (1:1, 8; 2:3), and he will say it three times (verses 20-22). It means whole, with integrity, not sinless.

decisions.choice: it would declare me crooked: my mouth, under the pressure of the trial
decisions.reason: The last verb can be read "it" (my mouth) or "he" (God). Read with the first line, Job's own mouth, confused and overpowered before God, would end up condemning him. If the subject is God, the sense is that God would twist his case.

decisions.choice: condemn: declare guilty
decisions.reason: The verb (rasha', causative) is the court word for finding someone in the wrong, the opposite of being in the right (tsadaq).

decisions.choice: my own words
decisions.reason: Readable says what "mouth" stands for here, the words Job would speak.

source.text: תָּֽם־אָ֭נִי לֹֽא־אֵדַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֗י אֶמְאַ֥ס חַיָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Blameless I [am]; not I know my soul; I reject my life.

en.L: I [am] blameless; I do not know my [own] self; \q I despise my life.
en.B: I am blameless, yet I no longer care about myself; \q I loathe my life.
en.R: I am blameless, but I do not care what happens to me. \q I hate my life.

es.L: Íntegro [soy] yo; no conozco mi [propia] alma; \q desprecio mi vida.
es.B: Soy íntegro, pero ya no me importa lo que sea de mí; \q aborrezco mi vida.
es.R: Soy íntegro, pero no me importa lo que me pase. \q Odio mi vida.

fr.L: Je [suis] intègre ; je ne connais pas mon [propre] être ; \q je méprise ma vie.
fr.B: Je suis intègre, et pourtant je ne me soucie plus de moi ; \q j’ai ma vie en dégoût.
fr.R: Je suis intègre, mais ce qui m’arrive m’est égal. \q Je déteste ma vie.

sw.L: Mimi [ni] mkamilifu; sijui nafsi yangu [mwenyewe]; \q nayadharau maisha yangu.
sw.B: Mimi ni mkamilifu, lakini sijali tena nafsi yangu; \q nayachukia maisha yangu.
sw.R: Mimi ni mkamilifu, lakini sijali litakalonipata. \q Nayachukia maisha yangu.

vi.L: Tôi [là người] trọn vẹn; tôi không biết [chính] bản thân tôi; \q tôi khinh ghét mạng sống mình.
vi.B: Tôi trọn vẹn, nhưng tôi chẳng còn thiết gì đến bản thân; \q tôi chán ghét đời mình.
vi.R: Tôi trọn vẹn, nhưng tôi chẳng còn quan tâm điều gì xảy đến cho mình. \q Tôi ghét cuộc đời mình.

ko.L: 나는 흠이 없다. 나는 내 [자신의] 영혼을 알지 못한다. \q 나는 내 생명을 멸시한다.
ko.B: 나는 흠이 없지만 이제 내 자신을 돌보지 않는다. \q 내 삶이 싫다.
ko.R: 나는 흠이 없지만 내게 무슨 일이 일어나든 상관없다. \q 나는 내 삶이 싫다.

decisions.choice: I do not know myself: I no longer care what becomes of me
decisions.reason: "Know" in Hebrew can mean to care for or to take note of (Genesis 39:6; Psalm 1:6). "I do not know my soul" most likely means Job no longer cares about his own life, which fits the next words. It can also mean that he does not understand himself.

decisions.choice: my soul: myself, my own life
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) here means the person himself.

decisions.choice: reject: despise, refuse
decisions.reason: The verb (ma'as) is the one Job used in 7:16, "I loathe it; I would not live forever."

source.text: אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֑רְתִּי תָּ֥ם וְ֝רָשָׁ֗ע ה֣וּא מְכַלֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: One [is] it; therefore I say: blameless and wicked he is bringing to an end.

en.L: It [is all] one; therefore I say, \q "The blameless and [the] wicked {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroys."
en.B: It is all the same; that is why I say, \q "He destroys both the blameless and the wicked."
en.R: It makes no difference. That is why I say, \q "God destroys good people and evil people alike."

es.L: [Todo] es uno; por eso digo: \q «Al íntegro y al malvado {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los destruye».
es.B: Todo da lo mismo; por eso digo: \q «Él destruye tanto al íntegro como al malvado».
es.R: No hay ninguna diferencia. Por eso digo: \q «Dios destruye por igual a los buenos y a los malos».

fr.L: C’[est tout] un ; c’est pourquoi je dis : \q « L’intègre et le méchant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les anéantit. »
fr.B: Tout revient au même ; voilà pourquoi je dis : \q « Il fait périr l’intègre comme le méchant. »
fr.R: Cela ne change rien. C’est pour ça que je dis : \q « Dieu détruit les bons comme les méchants. »

sw.L: [Yote ni] mamoja; kwa hiyo nasema, \q “Mkamilifu na mwovu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} huwaangamiza.”
sw.B: Ni sawa tu; ndiyo maana nasema, \q “Huwaangamiza wakamilifu na waovu pia.”
sw.R: Hakuna tofauti. Ndiyo sababu nasema, \q “Mungu huwaangamiza watu wema na watu waovu sawasawa.”

vi.L: [Mọi sự đều] như một; vì thế tôi nói: \q “Người trọn vẹn và kẻ ác {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đều tiêu diệt.”
vi.B: Mọi sự đều như nhau; vì thế tôi nói: \q “Ngài tiêu diệt cả người trọn vẹn lẫn kẻ ác.”
vi.R: Chẳng có gì khác biệt. Vì vậy tôi nói: \q “Đức Chúa Trời tiêu diệt người tốt cũng như kẻ ác.”

ko.L: [모든 것이] 매한가지다. 그러므로 내가 말한다. \q “흠 없는 자나 악한 자나 그분께서 멸하신다.”
ko.B: 모두 마찬가지다. 그래서 내가 말한다. \q “그분은 흠 없는 사람이나 악인이나 모두 멸하신다.”
ko.R: 아무런 차이가 없다. 그래서 나는 말한다. \q “하나님은 선한 사람이든 악한 사람이든 똑같이 멸하신다.”

decisions.choice: it is one: it is all the same
decisions.reason: "It is one" means it makes no difference: whether Job is blameless or not, the outcome will be the same.

decisions.choice: the blameless and the wicked he destroys: Job's charge against God's justice
decisions.reason: This is the boldest thing Job has said. The friends hold that God destroys only the wicked (4:7; 8:20, where Bildad says God will not reject a blameless man). Job says his own case proves the opposite. The book lets Job say it; God's reply comes in chapters 38-41, and in 42:7 God says Job spoke rightly of him, while the friends did not.

decisions.choice: bringing to an end: destroying, finishing off
decisions.reason: The verb (kalah) means to make an end of, to destroy completely.

source.text: אִם־שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג׃

records.literal_gloss: If a scourge kills suddenly, at [the] despair of innocent [ones] he mocks.

en.L: If a scourge kills suddenly, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mocks at the despair of [the] innocent.
en.B: When a disaster brings sudden death, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mocks at the despair of the innocent.
en.R: When disaster suddenly kills people, \q God laughs at the misery of the innocent.

es.L: Si un azote mata de repente, \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se burla de la desesperación de [los] inocentes.
es.B: Cuando una desgracia trae muerte repentina, \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se burla de la angustia de los inocentes.
es.R: Cuando una calamidad mata de repente a la gente, \q Dios se ríe de la desgracia de los inocentes.

fr.L: Si un fléau tue soudain, \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se moque du désespoir des innocents.
fr.B: Quand un désastre fait périr d’un coup, \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se moque du désespoir des innocents.
fr.R: Quand un malheur tue des gens d’un coup, \q Dieu rit de la détresse des innocents.

sw.L: Ikiwa pigo laua ghafula, \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hudhihaki kukata tamaa kwa wasio na hatia.
sw.B: Maafa yanapoleta kifo cha ghafula, \q huidhihaki hofu ya wasio na hatia.
sw.R: Maafa yanapowaua watu ghafla, \q Mungu huicheka taabu ya wasio na hatia.

vi.L: Nếu roi tai họa giết chết bất thình lình, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chế nhạo nỗi tuyệt vọng của [người] vô tội.
vi.B: Khi tai họa gây chết chóc thình lình, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chế nhạo nỗi tuyệt vọng của người vô tội.
vi.R: Khi tai họa bất ngờ giết chết người ta, \q Đức Chúa Trời cười nhạo nỗi khổ của người vô tội.

ko.L: 재앙의 채찍이 갑자기 죽일 때에, \q 그분은 죄 없는 자들의 절망을 비웃으신다.
ko.B: 재앙이 닥쳐 갑자기 죽음이 덮칠 때에 \q 그분은 죄 없는 사람들의 절망을 비웃으신다.
ko.R: 재앙이 갑자기 사람들을 죽일 때, \q 하나님은 죄 없는 사람들의 고통을 보고 웃으신다.

decisions.choice: a scourge: a whip, here a disaster that strikes
decisions.reason: The word (shot) is a whip; in poetry it is a disaster that lashes people (5:21; Isaiah 28:15).

decisions.choice: despair: the melting away of courage
decisions.reason: The word (massat) appears only here. It most likely comes from the verb for melting, so it is despair or dismay. If it comes from the verb for testing, it is the trial of the innocent. Either way God is pictured as mocking innocent people in their suffering.

decisions.choice: he mocks: Job's bitter exaggeration
decisions.reason: Job speaks out of pain and puts the worst construction on what has happened to him. The friends will take such words as proof that he is wicked (15:5-6); the book records them as the cry of a man who still addresses God.

decisions.choice: laughs at
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for mocking.

source.text: אֶ֤רֶץ׀נִתְּנָ֬ה בְֽיַד־רָשָׁ֗ע פְּנֵֽי־שֹׁפְטֶ֥יהָ יְכַסֶּ֑ה אִם־לֹ֖א אֵפ֣וֹא מִי־הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] earth has been given into [the] hand of a wicked [one]; [the] faces of its judges he covers; if not, then who [is] he?

en.L: [The] earth has been given into [the] hand of [the] wicked; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} covers the faces of its judges; \q if not [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}], then who is it?
en.B: The earth is handed over to the wicked; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blindfolds its judges. \q If it is not {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, then who is it?
en.R: The world has been handed over to evil people. \q God covers the eyes of its judges so they cannot see what is right. \q If it is not God who does this, who is it?

es.L: [La] tierra ha sido entregada en mano del malvado; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} cubre los rostros de sus jueces; \q si no [es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}], ¿quién es entonces?
es.B: La tierra queda en manos de los malvados; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} venda los ojos de sus jueces. \q Si no es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, ¿quién es?
es.R: El mundo ha sido entregado a la gente malvada. \q Dios tapa los ojos de sus jueces para que no vean lo que es justo. \q Si no es Dios quien hace esto, ¿quién es?

fr.L: [La] terre a été livrée à [la] main du méchant ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} couvre la face de ses juges ; \q si ce n’est [pas {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], qui est-ce donc ?
fr.B: La terre est livrée aux méchants ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} bande les yeux de ses juges. \q Si ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, qui est-ce ?
fr.R: Le monde a été livré aux méchants. \q Dieu couvre les yeux de ses juges pour qu’ils ne voient pas ce qui est juste. \q Si ce n’est pas Dieu qui fait cela, qui est-ce ?

sw.L: Nchi imetiwa mkononi mwa mwovu; \q hufunika nyuso za waamuzi wake; \q kama si [{{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}], basi ni nani?
sw.B: Dunia imekabidhiwa kwa waovu; \q huwafunga waamuzi wake vitambaa machoni. \q Kama si {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, basi ni nani?
sw.R: Ulimwengu umekabidhiwa kwa watu waovu. \q Mungu huyafunika macho ya waamuzi wake ili wasione lililo sawa. \q Kama si Mungu anayefanya hivyo, ni nani basi?

vi.L: Đất đã bị phó vào tay kẻ ác; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} che mặt các thẩm phán của nó; \q nếu không [phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}], thì là ai?
vi.B: Đất bị trao vào tay kẻ ác; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bịt mắt các thẩm phán của nó. \q Nếu không phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì còn ai nữa?
vi.R: Thế gian đã bị giao vào tay kẻ ác. \q Đức Chúa Trời che mắt các quan tòa để họ không thấy điều phải. \q Nếu không phải Đức Chúa Trời làm việc này, thì là ai?

ko.L: 땅이 악인의 손에 넘겨졌고, \q 그분께서 그 재판관들의 얼굴을 가리신다. \q 그분이 아니라면 누구란 말이냐?
ko.B: 세상은 악인들의 손에 넘어갔고, \q 그분께서 재판관들의 눈을 가리신다. \q 그분이 아니시라면 대체 누구냐?
ko.R: 세상은 악한 사람들에게 넘겨졌다. \q 하나님께서 재판관들의 눈을 가리셔서 옳은 것을 보지 못하게 하신다. \q 이 일을 하시는 분이 하나님이 아니라면 누구겠느냐?

decisions.choice: the earth: the world, or the land
decisions.reason: The word ('erets) can be the whole earth or a land; here the complaint is general, about the world as Job sees it.

decisions.choice: he covers: God
decisions.reason: The subject of "covers" could be the wicked one, who corrupts the judges. The last line, "if not he, then who?", shows that Job means God: he holds God responsible for injustice in the world.

decisions.choice: covers the faces of its judges: makes them blind to justice
decisions.reason: To cover someone's face is to blindfold them; judges who cannot see do not judge rightly (compare Exodus 23:8, a bribe blinds the clear-sighted).

decisions.choice: blindfolds
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English word for what covering the face does (m3).

decisions.choice: so they cannot see what is right; God who does this
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture (m3) and the subject (m2).

source.text: וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־רָ֑ץ בָּֽ֝רְח֗וּ לֹא־רָא֥וּ טוֹבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And my days are swifter than a runner; they flee, not they see good.

en.L: And my days are swifter than a runner; \q they flee away, they do not see good.
en.B: My days go by faster than a runner; \q they slip away without seeing anything good.
en.R: My days rush past faster than a man running with a message. \q They hurry away, and I see nothing good in them.

es.L: Y mis días son más veloces que un corredor; \q huyen, no ven el bien.
es.B: Mis días pasan más rápido que un correo; \q se escapan sin ver nada bueno.
es.R: Mis días pasan más rápido que un hombre que corre con un mensaje. \q Se van a toda prisa, y no veo nada bueno en ellos.

fr.L: Et mes jours sont plus rapides qu’un coureur ; \q ils s’enfuient, ils ne voient pas le bonheur.
fr.B: Mes jours filent plus vite qu’un messager ; \q ils s’échappent sans avoir rien vu de bon.
fr.R: Mes jours passent plus vite qu’un homme qui court porter un message. \q Ils s’en vont à toute allure, et je n’y vois rien de bon.

sw.L: Na siku zangu ni za upesi kuliko tarishi; \q zinakimbia, hazioni mema.
sw.B: Siku zangu zinapita mbio kuliko tarishi; \q zinatoweka bila kuona jema lolote.
sw.R: Siku zangu zinapita kasi kuliko mtu anayekimbia na ujumbe. \q Zinaondoka haraka, wala sioni jema lolote ndani yake.

vi.L: Và những ngày của tôi nhanh hơn người chạy trạm; \q chúng trốn đi, chẳng thấy điều tốt lành.
vi.B: Những ngày đời tôi qua nhanh hơn người đưa tin; \q chúng vụt mất mà chẳng thấy được điều gì tốt đẹp.
vi.R: Những ngày của tôi trôi qua nhanh hơn người chạy đưa thư. \q Chúng vội vã qua đi, và tôi chẳng thấy điều gì tốt đẹp trong đó.

ko.L: 내 날들은 달리는 자보다 빠르니, \q 달아나 버리고 좋은 것을 보지 못한다.
ko.B: 내 날들은 파발꾼보다 빨리 지나가니, \q 좋은 것 하나 보지 못하고 사라져 버린다.
ko.R: 내 날들은 소식을 들고 달려가는 사람보다 더 빨리 지나간다. \q 서둘러 사라져 버리고, 나는 그 안에서 좋은 것을 하나도 보지 못한다.

decisions.choice: a runner: a courier carrying messages
decisions.reason: The runner (rats) was a royal messenger who ran on foot with dispatches (2 Samuel 18:19-23; Esther 3:13, 15). Job's days pass as fast as such a man.

decisions.choice: not see good: have no happiness
decisions.reason: "See good" means to experience good things (7:7, "my eye will not again see good").

decisions.choice: the speed of life: three pictures
decisions.reason: Verses 25-26 give three pictures of speed, on land (a runner), on water (reed boats) and in the air (an eagle). Job said in 7:6 that his days were swifter than a weaver's shuttle.

decisions.choice: a man running with a message
decisions.reason: Readable says who the runner is (m1).

source.text: חָ֭לְפוּ עִם־אֳנִיּ֣וֹת אֵבֶ֑ה כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר יָט֥וּשׂ עֲלֵי־אֹֽכֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: They pass by with ships of reed, like an eagle swooping on food.

en.L: They pass by like ships of reed, \q like an eagle swooping on prey.
en.B: They glide past like boats made of reeds, \q like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
en.R: They speed by like light reed boats on a river, \q like an eagle diving down to catch its food.

es.L: Pasan como barcas de junco, \q como águila que se lanza sobre la presa.
es.B: Se deslizan como barcas hechas de juncos, \q como el águila que se abalanza sobre su presa.
es.R: Pasan veloces como ligeras barcas de junco en un río, \q como un águila que baja en picada para atrapar su comida.

fr.L: Ils passent comme des barques de jonc, \q comme un aigle qui fond sur sa proie.
fr.B: Ils glissent comme des barques de roseaux, \q comme l’aigle qui fond sur sa proie.
fr.R: Ils filent comme de légères barques de roseaux sur un fleuve, \q comme un aigle qui plonge pour attraper sa nourriture.

sw.L: Zinapita kama mashua za mafunjo, \q kama tai ashukaye juu ya mawindo.
sw.B: Zinateleza kama mashua zilizotengenezwa kwa mafunjo, \q kama tai anayeshuka kwa kasi juu ya mawindo yake.
sw.R: Zinapita kwa kasi kama mashua nyepesi za mafunjo mtoni, \q kama tai anayeshuka chini kukamata chakula chake.

vi.L: Chúng lướt qua như những thuyền bằng sậy, \q như chim đại bàng sà xuống con mồi.
vi.B: Chúng lướt qua như những chiếc thuyền làm bằng sậy, \q như chim đại bàng lao xuống vồ mồi.
vi.R: Chúng trôi vụt qua như những chiếc thuyền sậy nhẹ trên sông, \q như chim đại bàng bổ nhào xuống bắt mồi.

ko.L: 그것들이 갈대배처럼 지나가고, \q 먹이를 덮치는 독수리 같다.
ko.B: 내 날들은 갈대로 엮은 배처럼 미끄러져 가고, \q 먹이를 덮치려고 내리꽂히는 독수리 같다.
ko.R: 내 날들은 강 위를 달리는 가벼운 갈대배처럼 빨리 지나가고, \q 먹이를 잡으려고 내리꽂히는 독수리처럼 지나간다.

decisions.choice: ships of reed: light, fast papyrus boats
decisions.reason: Boats made of bundled papyrus reeds were light and swift on the Nile (Isaiah 18:2 speaks of "vessels of papyrus on the waters"). The word for reed ('eveh) is found only here.

decisions.choice: eagle: a great bird of prey
decisions.reason: The word (nesher) covers the great birds of prey, the eagle and the griffon vulture. The point is the speed of its dive.

decisions.choice: food: prey
decisions.reason: The word means food; for a bird of prey, the animal it catches.

decisions.choice: like ships
decisions.reason: The Hebrew preposition is "with": the days pass along with, that is as fast as, the reed boats. Literal uses "like" for clarity, to match the second line.

source.text: אִם־אָ֭מְרִי אֶשְׁכְּחָ֣ה שִׂיחִ֑י אֶעֶזְבָ֖ה פָנַ֣י וְאַבְלִֽיגָה׃

records.literal_gloss: If my saying [is], I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my face and be cheerful,

en.L: If I say, "I will forget my complaint, \q I will put off my [sad] face and be cheerful,"
en.B: If I say, "I will forget my complaint; \q I will put away my sad face and smile,"
en.R: I may say, "I will forget my complaints. \q I will stop looking sad and try to be cheerful."

es.L: Si digo: «Olvidaré mi queja, \q dejaré mi rostro [triste] y me alegraré»,
es.B: Si digo: «Olvidaré mi queja; \q dejaré mi cara triste y sonreiré»,
es.R: Puedo decir: «Me olvidaré de mis quejas. \q Dejaré de poner cara triste y trataré de estar alegre».

fr.L: Si je dis : « J’oublierai ma plainte, \q je quitterai mon visage [triste] et je serai joyeux »,
fr.B: Si je dis : « J’oublierai ma plainte ; \q je quitterai ma mine triste et je sourirai »,
fr.R: Je peux bien dire : « Je vais oublier mes plaintes. \q Je vais arrêter d’avoir l’air triste et essayer d’être joyeux. »

sw.L: Nikisema, “Nitayasahau malalamiko yangu, \q nitaiacha sura yangu [ya huzuni] na kuchangamka,”
sw.B: Nikisema, “Nitayasahau malalamiko yangu; \q nitaiondoa sura ya huzuni na kutabasamu,”
sw.R: Huenda nikasema, “Nitayasahau malalamiko yangu. \q Nitaacha kuonekana mwenye huzuni na kujaribu kuchangamka.”

vi.L: Nếu tôi nói: “Tôi sẽ quên lời than thở của mình, \q tôi sẽ bỏ nét mặt [buồn] và tươi tỉnh lên,”
vi.B: Nếu tôi nói: “Tôi sẽ quên đi nỗi than phiền; \q tôi sẽ gạt bỏ vẻ mặt buồn bã và mỉm cười,”
vi.R: Tôi có thể nói: “Tôi sẽ quên những lời than thở của mình. \q Tôi sẽ thôi buồn rầu và cố gắng vui lên.”

ko.L: “내 탄식을 잊고, \q 내 [슬픈] 얼굴을 버리고 밝게 지내리라” 하고 말해도,
ko.B: “내 탄식을 잊어버리고 \q 슬픈 얼굴을 버리고 웃으리라” 하고 말해 보아도,
ko.R: “이제 불평은 잊어버리자. \q 슬픈 얼굴은 그만하고 밝게 지내 보자” 하고 말해 볼 수도 있다.

decisions.choice: leave off my face: change one's sad expression
decisions.reason: "Abandon my face" means to put away a sad or gloomy look (compare 1 Samuel 1:18, where Hannah's face "was no longer" sad).

decisions.choice: be cheerful: brighten up, smile
decisions.reason: The verb (balag) means to brighten, to cheer up; Job uses it again in 10:20, and it is found in Psalm 39:14.

decisions.choice: complaint: my troubled speech, my lament
decisions.reason: The word (siach) is meditation or complaint, the pouring out of trouble (7:13; 10:1).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 28
decisions.reason: Verse 27 is the "if" half of a sentence finished in verse 28, so Literal and Balanced end it with a comma. Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

source.text: יָגֹ֥רְתִּי כָל־עַצְּבֹתָ֑י יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־לֹ֥א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: I dread all my pains; I know that not you will hold me innocent.

en.L: I dread all my sufferings; \q I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not hold me innocent.
en.B: I am still afraid of all my pains, \q for I know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not declare me innocent.
en.R: But I am still afraid of all my pain. \q I know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not say I am innocent.

es.L: temo todos mis sufrimientos; \q sé que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no me tendrás por inocente.
es.B: aún temo todos mis dolores, \q porque sé que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no me declararás inocente.
es.R: Pero sigo teniendo miedo de todo mi dolor. \q Sé que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no dirás que soy inocente.

fr.L: je redoute toutes mes souffrances ; \q je sais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne me tiendras pas pour innocent.
fr.B: j’ai encore peur de toutes mes douleurs, \q car je sais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne me déclareras pas innocent.
fr.R: Mais j’ai toujours peur de toute ma douleur. \q Je sais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne diras pas que je suis innocent.

sw.L: ninaogopa maumivu yangu yote; \q najua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hutanihesabu kuwa sina hatia.
