sw.B: bado nayaogopa maumivu yangu yote, \q kwa maana najua {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hutanitangaza kuwa sina hatia.
sw.R: Lakini bado naogopa maumivu yangu yote. \q Najua {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hutasema kwamba sina hatia.

vi.L: thì con sợ hãi mọi nỗi đau đớn của con; \q con biết rằng Chúa sẽ không xem con là vô tội.
vi.B: con vẫn sợ hãi mọi nỗi đau của mình, \q vì con biết Chúa sẽ không tuyên bố con vô tội.
vi.R: Nhưng con vẫn sợ mọi nỗi đau của con. \q Con biết Chúa sẽ không nói rằng con vô tội.

ko.L: 저는 저의 모든 고통이 두렵습니다. \q 주님께서 저를 죄 없다 하지 않으실 줄 압니다.
ko.B: 저는 여전히 제 모든 고통이 두렵습니다. \q 주님께서 저를 죄 없다고 선언하지 않으실 줄 알기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그래도 저는 여전히 제 모든 아픔이 두렵습니다. \q 주님께서 저를 죄 없다고 하지 않으실 것을 압니다.

decisions.choice: you: Job turns from speaking about God to speaking to him
decisions.reason: Until here Job has spoken of God as "he". Now he speaks to God directly, as he will through chapter 10.

decisions.choice: hold me innocent: acquit me
decisions.reason: The verb (naqah) means to declare free of guilt, to let off unpunished (10:14; Exodus 34:7). Job expects God to treat him as guilty whatever he does.

decisions.choice: my pains: my sufferings
decisions.reason: The word ('atsevet) is pain or grief, of body or mind.

decisions.choice: still; for
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the link to verse 27 plain: even if he tries to cheer up, his dread remains, because he knows God's verdict.

decisions.choice: Job turns to God: "Chúa" for "you" and "con" for himself (9:28-31), then "tôi" again from 9:32
decisions.reason: Job speaks to God directly here for the first time in the speech (m1). He takes the address of the Psalms' laments, "Chúa" and "con"; when he speaks about God again (9:32-35) he says "tôi". "Tôi" before God is possible in so bitter a speech, so the choice is marked uncertain.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 with 주님 and 저 in 9:28-31; the plain style with 나 again from 9:32
decisions.reason: Job turns from speaking about God to speaking to him (m1), so he takes the polite prayer style of the Psalms' laments; when he speaks of God in the third person again (9:32-35) the plain style returns. Verse 27 is kept without a subject pronoun so the sentence can pass from one to the other.

source.text: אָנֹכִ֥י אֶרְשָׁ֑ע לָמָּה־זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל אִיגָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: I will be guilty; why this, [in] vain should I toil?

en.L: I will be [found] guilty; \q why then should I toil in vain?
en.B: I am going to be found guilty anyway; \q why then should I struggle in vain?
en.R: I will be judged guilty no matter what I do. \q So why should I even try?

es.L: Yo seré [hallado] culpable; \q ¿para qué, pues, fatigarme en vano?
es.B: De todos modos voy a ser declarado culpable; \q ¿para qué esforzarme en vano?
es.R: Me declararán culpable haga lo que haga. \q Entonces, ¿para qué intentarlo siquiera?

fr.L: Moi, je serai [déclaré] coupable ; \q pourquoi donc me fatiguer en vain ?
fr.B: De toute façon, je serai déclaré coupable ; \q pourquoi donc me donner de la peine pour rien ?
fr.R: Quoi que je fasse, je serai jugé coupable. \q Alors pourquoi même essayer ?

sw.L: Mimi nitaonekana [kuwa] na hatia; \q basi kwa nini nijitaabishe bure?
sw.B: Hata hivyo nitahukumiwa kuwa na hatia; \q basi kwa nini nijisumbue bure?
sw.R: Nitahukumiwa kuwa na hatia, hata nifanye nini. \q Basi kwa nini hata nijaribu?

vi.L: Con sẽ bị [kể là] có tội; \q vậy sao con phải nhọc công vô ích?
vi.B: Đằng nào con cũng bị kết tội; \q vậy sao con phải vất vả vô ích?
vi.R: Dù con làm gì, con cũng sẽ bị xử là có tội. \q Vậy con cố gắng làm gì?

ko.L: 저는 죄 있다 [판결을 받을] 것입니다. \q 그런데 어찌하여 제가 헛되이 수고하겠습니까?
ko.B: 어차피 저는 죄인으로 판결받을 것입니다. \q 그런데 왜 헛되이 애를 쓰겠습니까?
ko.R: 제가 무엇을 하든 죄인으로 판결받을 것입니다. \q 그러니 애써 볼 까닭이 무엇이겠습니까?

decisions.choice: I will be guilty: I am bound to be condemned
decisions.reason: The verb (rasha') here means to be counted guilty in court, not to be a wicked person. Job is sure the verdict is already fixed.

decisions.choice: in vain: for nothing, as useless as breath
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) is breath or vapor, something without substance; it is the key word of Ecclesiastes. Job said his days were hevel (7:16).

decisions.choice: toil: wear myself out
decisions.reason: The verb (yaga') is to labor or grow weary. Job means all his efforts to clear his name.

source.text: אִם־הִתְרָחַ֥צְתִּי בְמֵי־שָׁ֑לֶג וַ֝הֲזִכּ֗וֹתִי בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפָּֽי׃

decisions.choice: with snow water: the reading of the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The written text has a word meaning "in" or "with" (bemo), so "with snow"; the margin tells the reader to read "in the water of" snow. The sense is the same: Job washes with the purest water he can find.

decisions.choice: lye: an alkali for washing
decisions.reason: The word (bor) is lye or potash, the alkali made from plant ash and used to clean (Jeremiah 2:22, with the related word borit; Malachi 3:2).

decisions.choice: clean hands: innocence
decisions.reason: Clean hands stand for a clear conscience and an innocent life (17:9; 22:30; Psalm 24:4). Job means that however he proves himself innocent, God will make him filthy again (verse 31).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 31
decisions.reason: Verse 30 is the "if" half of a sentence finished in verse 31, so every level ends it with a comma.

decisions.choice: strong soap
decisions.reason: Readable uses a familiar word for the cleanser (m2).

en.R: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would still throw me into a muddy ditch. \q Even my clothes would be disgusted with me.

sw.L: ndipo {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ungenitumbukiza shimoni, \q na mavazi yangu mwenyewe yangenichukia.
sw.B: hata hivyo ungenitumbukiza katika shimo la uchafu, \q hata mavazi yangu mwenyewe yangenichukia.
sw.R: {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} bado ungenitupa katika shimo la matope. \q Hata nguo zangu zingenichukia.

vi.L: thì Chúa sẽ nhận con xuống [cái] hố, \q và chính áo xống con sẽ ghê tởm con.
vi.B: thì Chúa vẫn nhận con xuống hố bùn nhơ, \q đến nỗi chính áo xống con cũng ghê tởm con.
vi.R: thì Chúa vẫn sẽ ném con xuống mương bùn. \q Ngay cả quần áo của con cũng ghê sợ con.

ko.L: 주님께서 저를 구덩이에 빠뜨리실 것이니, \q 제 옷조차 저를 싫어할 것입니다.
ko.B: 그래도 주님께서는 저를 더러운 구덩이에 처넣으셔서 \q 제 옷마저 저를 역겨워할 것입니다.
ko.R: 주님께서는 여전히 저를 진흙 구덩이에 던지실 것입니다. \q 그러면 제 옷조차 저를 보고 역겨워할 것입니다.

decisions.choice: the pit: a ditch, a muddy hole
decisions.reason: The word (shachat) is a pit, often the grave (17:14; 33:18). Here, after washing, it is a filthy ditch: whatever Job does to make himself clean, God would plunge him back into the mud.

decisions.choice: my clothes would abhor me: I would be so filthy even my clothes would recoil
decisions.reason: The clothes are spoken of as if they could feel disgust, a picture of utter filth.

decisions.choice: you (lowercase): the sentence continues verse 30
decisions.reason: Readable starts this record mid-sentence, after the comma that ends verse 30, so "you" is lowercase and keeps its setting span.

source.text: כִּי־לֹא־אִ֣ישׁ כָּמֹ֣נִי אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ נָב֥וֹא יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: For not a man like me [is he], I would answer him; we would come together into judgment.

en.L: For [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] not a man like me, that I might answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q that we might come together in judgment.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not a human being like me, that I could answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q that we could go to court together.
en.R: God is not a human like me. \q I cannot argue with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} or take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to court.

es.L: Porque [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no es] un hombre como yo, para que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} responda, \q para que vayamos juntos a juicio.

vi.L: Vì [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] không phải là người như tôi, để tôi đáp lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q để chúng tôi cùng nhau ra trước tòa xét xử.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không phải là con người như tôi, để tôi có thể đối đáp với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q để hai bên cùng ra tòa.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời không phải là con người như tôi. \q Tôi không thể tranh luận với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hay kiện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra tòa.

ko.L: 그분은 나 같은 사람이 아니시므로 내가 그분께 대답하거나 \q 우리가 함께 재판정에 나갈 수 없다.

decisions.choice: a man: a human being
decisions.reason: The word ('ish) here sets God against humans: God is not a mortal Job could meet on equal terms (compare Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29).

decisions.choice: judgment: a court case, a trial
decisions.reason: The word (mishpat) here means a legal hearing; to come together in judgment is for two parties to meet before a judge.

decisions.choice: two plain sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the verse into two short sentences and says plainly what answering him and coming together in judgment mean: arguing a case in court.

records.literal_gloss: Not there is between us an arbiter, [who] would set his hand upon [the] two of us.

es.R: No hay nadie que pueda ponerse entre nosotros \q y resolver el caso para los dos.

fr.L: Il n’y a pas entre nous d’arbitre \q [qui] pose sa main sur [nous] deux.
fr.B: Il n’y a personne pour juger entre nous, \q qui puisse poser la main sur nous deux.
fr.R: Il n’y a personne qui puisse se placer entre nous \q et régler l’affaire pour nous deux.

ko.L: 우리 사이에 중재자가 없다. \q 우리 둘 위에 손을 얹을 [이가 없다].
ko.B: 우리 사이를 판가름해 줄 이가 없다. \q 우리 둘 모두에게 손을 얹을 이가 없다.
ko.R: 우리 사이에 서 줄 사람이 아무도 없다. \q 우리 둘의 문제를 해결해 줄 사람이 없다.

decisions.choice: an arbiter: one who decides between two parties
decisions.reason: The word (mokhiach) is one who sets things right, who reproves or decides between two people (Isaiah 2:4; Genesis 31:37). Job wants a third party with authority over God and himself alike. He will long for such a one again in 16:19-21 and 19:25.

decisions.choice: there is no: the Hebrew vowels; "if only there were" with other vowels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "there is not" (lo'). Read with different vowels (lu), the same letters say "if only there were", and some ancient translations read so. Both readings say no arbiter exists.

decisions.choice: set his hand on the two of us: have authority over both
decisions.reason: To lay a hand on both parties pictures someone who can bring both to order and make them keep the decision.

decisions.choice: settle the case for both of us
alternatives: lay his hand on us both
decisions.reason: Readable says what laying a hand on both parties means (m3).

source.text: יָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י שִׁבְט֑וֹ וְ֝אֵמָת֗וֹ אַֽל־תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃

en.B: Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} take {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rod off me, \q and let the dread of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} no longer terrify me;
en.R: If only God would stop beating me, \q and stop frightening me,

es.B: Que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quite de encima de mí {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vara, \q y que el pavor que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} inspira no me aterre más;
es.R: Si tan solo Dios dejara de golpearme \q y dejara de asustarme,

fr.L: Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} écarte de moi {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} bâton, \q et que {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} terreur ne m’effraie pas ;
fr.B: Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} retire {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} bâton de dessus moi, \q et que la crainte qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} inspire ne m’épouvante plus ;
fr.R: Si seulement Dieu arrêtait de me frapper \q et de me faire peur,

sw.L: Na aiondoe fimbo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yangu, \q na utisho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usinitie hofu;
sw.B: Na aiondoe fimbo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yangu, \q na hofu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} isinitishe tena;
sw.R: Laiti Mungu angeacha kunipiga \q na kuacha kunitisha,

vi.L: Nguyện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cất cây roi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khỏi tôi, \q và sự kinh khiếp từ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đừng làm tôi sợ hãi;
vi.B: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cất cây roi khỏi tôi, \q và nỗi kinh hoàng về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không còn làm tôi khiếp sợ,

ko.B: 그분께서 그분의 매를 내게서 거두시고, \q 그분에 대한 두려움이 더는 나를 떨게 하지 않는다면,
ko.R: 하나님께서 나를 그만 때리시고 \q 나를 그만 겁주신다면,

decisions.choice: his rod: God's punishing hand
decisions.reason: The rod (shevet) is the stick used to beat and punish (21:9; Proverbs 13:24). Job means the suffering God has sent.

decisions.choice: let him remove: Job's condition for a fair hearing
decisions.reason: Verses 34-35 say what would have to happen for Job to speak freely: God would have to stop striking and terrifying him. Job asks the same in 13:21.

decisions.choice: his terror: the dread God inspires
decisions.reason: The word ('emah) is fear or terror; it is the terror that comes from God (13:21; 33:7).

decisions.choice: stop beating me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the rod stands for (m1).

records.literal_gloss: I would speak and not fear him, for not so I [am] with myself.

fr.R: alors je pourrais parler sans avoir peur de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \q Mais vu comment sont les choses, je ne peux pas.

sw.L: [Ndipo] ningesema wala nisimwogope, \q kwa maana mimi si hivyo nafsini mwangu.

vi.L: [Thì] tôi sẽ nói mà không sợ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q vì tôi không như thế với chính mình.
vi.B: thì tôi sẽ nói mà không sợ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Nhưng trong tình cảnh của tôi bây giờ, tôi không thể.
vi.R: thì tôi có thể nói mà không sợ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Nhưng như mọi sự hiện nay, tôi không thể.

ko.L: [그러면] 내가 말하고 그분을 두려워하지 않을 것이다. \q 나는 내 자신에게 그렇지 않기 때문이다.
ko.B: 나는 그분을 두려워하지 않고 말할 것이다. \q 그러나 지금 내 형편으로는 그럴 수 없다.
ko.R: 나는 그분을 두려워하지 않고 말할 수 있을 것이다. \q 그러나 지금 형편으로는 그럴 수가 없다.

decisions.choice: not so I am with myself: as things stand with me, I cannot
alternatives: I am not like that in myself
I know I am not guilty
decisions.reason: The last line is short and hard: "for not so I with myself". It most likely means that, as things are now, Job is not able to speak without fear. It may instead mean "I am not what you think I am", that is, Job knows himself to be innocent, or "in myself I am not afraid".

decisions.choice: I would speak: the result if God withdrew his rod
decisions.reason: This verse completes verse 34: if God took away the rod and the terror, Job would speak.

decisions.choice: But as things are with me, I cannot
alternatives: for I am not so with myself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the most likely sense (m1) in a plain sentence; the footnote gives the others.
